Biological secondary treatment consists of aeration basins and secondary clarifiers in two parallel treatment trains with a combined capacity of 8.0 MGD.
Biological secondary treatment consists of aeration basins and secondary clarifiers in two parallel treatment trains with a combined capacity of 8.0 MGD.
Primary-treated wastewater over 8.0 MGD is directed to one rotating biological contactor followed by secondary clarifiers, or to flow equalization.
The basins (previously used for two decommissioned rotating biological contactor trains) provide an additional 0.46 million gallons of flow equalization capacity.

During peak flows or upsets, the plant can store up to one million gallons of influent, primary effluent, or final effluent in seven flow equalization and storage basins, called multi-purpose storage basins, for later treatment.
All secondary-treated effluent is combined in the chlorine mixing chamber and disinfected and dechlorinated prior to discharge.
